newsitem.title: INDIA: India to import over 70 pct of its oil by 2010.
newsitem.headline: India to import over 70 pct of its oil by 2010.

text.p: India's dependence on oil imports is set to rise, with more than 70 percent of its needs being met by imports by 2010, against 60 percent currently, an International Energy Agency official said on Tuesday.

"World oil demand will grow somewhat faster in the future than over the past two decades," IEA deputy executive director John Ferriter told an international conference on oil and gas in the Indian capital.
"Oil demand should increase from around 72 milion barrels per day in 1996 to between 92 and 97 million barrels per day in 2010," he added.
Ferriter forecast that South Asia-- comprising Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka -- would see a rapid increase in oil demand.
As the largest consumer in this region, India would account for about 15 percent of global demand growth by 2010, he said.
"Imports represent 60 percent of Indian oil consumption today and are expected to reach more than 70 percent by 2010, and increasingly from Middle Eastern sources," Ferriter added.

Growth in oil demand, combined with recently stagnating and uncertain future trends in domestic crude production, will "inevitably" lead to an increase in India's dependence on external oil sources, he said. -- Clarence Fernandez, New Delhi newsroom +91-11-301 2024
